faqs.question: What does the Fungal Identification – Pure Culture test measure?
faqs.answer: This test helps identify the fungal species present in a sample.

faqs.question: Why is the Fungal Identification – Pure Culture test done?
faqs.answer: The Fungal Identification – Pure Culture test is done for the following reasons: • To determine the specific fungus or fungal isolate causing an infection, enabling targeted treatment • To guide appropriate antifungal therapy • To monitor the effectiveness of treatment • To identify potential drug resistance in fungal isolates

faqs.question: When is the Fungal Identification – Pure Culture test recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: The Fungal Identification – Pure Culture test may be recommended if you • Have symptoms suggestive of a fungal infection, such as persistent cough, skin rashes, or recurrent vaginal infections. • Have a weakened immune system due to conditions like HIV/AIDS or undergoing organ transplantation. • Have undergone previous treatment for a fungal infection to assess treatment response.

faqs.question: What if the results of the Fungal Identification – Pure Culture test are abnormal?
faqs.answer: Abnormal results from the Fungal Identification – Pure Culture test may indicate • A specific fungal infection that requires targeted treatment. • Antifungal resistance, which may require alternative medications. • Co-infection with multiple types of fungi, necessitating adjusted treatment strategies.

faqs.question: What to expect during the Fungal Identification – Pure Culture test?
faqs.answer: During this test, a sample of the site suspected to be infected with fungus will be collected, typically in the form of a swab or biopsy. The same will then be sent for analysis to identify the specific fungal isolate.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the Fungal Identification – Pure Culture test?
faqs.answer: To prepare for this test: • Your doctor may advise you to stop certain medications that can interfere with test results. • Follow any dietary restrictions or fasting instructions given before the test. • Inform your doctor about any recent antifungal treatments or use of topical creams on the affected area. Please reach out to your healthcare provider for any specific requirements.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with the Fungal Identification – Pure Culture test?
faqs.answer: Other tests that may be ordered alongside the Fungal Identification – Pure Culture test include: • Fungal Sensitivity Testing: This test determines the effectiveness of different antifungal medications against the identified fungal isolate. • Histopathology: A microscopic examination of tissue samples to assess the extent of fungal infection and identify any potential complications.

faqs.question: What is the Fungal Identification – Pure Culture test also known as?
What is a fungal infection?
faqs.answer: A fungal infection occurs when harmful fungi invade various parts of the body, leading to symptoms such as skin rashes, nail changes, respiratory problems, or genital infections. Prompt diagnosis and treatment are essential to prevent complications.
